verdict.coupling_note: wealth_redistribution shock moves the behavioural benchmarks; previously all four were 0.0000 delta
verdict.intended_mechanism_note: the wealth-scale on U_accept is a real second-order effect but is dominated by selection (reject -> poor) and by Q-learning
verdict.flag_retirement_justification: wealth enters the decision path; the [WEALTH-INERT-IN-DECISION-LOOP] flag is retired because wealth is no longer ignored by the accept rule

scientific_finding: In this engine, the population-level correlation between wealth and rejection rate is dominated by selection: rejecting offers prevents earning, so rejection causes poverty. The intended mechanism (diminishing marginal utility under wealth) exists in the code but is second-order relative to selection. This is an emergent property of the calibrated engine, not a modelling error.
engineering_consequence: Any scenario that involves wealth dynamics now produces behavioural effects. The engine no longer treats wealth as a passive accumulator. This unlocks meaningful wealth-intervention experiments, with the caveat that the observed direction in a given scenario is an empirical outcome, not a design intent.
